information_set.rule: docs/decisions/information-set.md rule 1: the daily NY Fed rates are read at the row two panel days before the target T. A forecast for lead h from decision day D therefore knows the spread outcomes up to the panel day D - 1 (target T = D + h), and not the outcome of D. 'Public at the decision' below means: the outcome of a target on a panel day at or before D - 1
information_set.consequence: the hit of target D (a lead-1 cell of decision day D - 1) is not public at decision day D, so no adjustment may feed the previous day's hit or residual into the forecast of D + 1; the most recent public lead-1 error is the one for target D - 1. The tables that use the previous day's outcome (lag 1) are diagnostics of structure and are marked 'not public'

tables.where: the 11 Holm-rejected cells of the design, and the independence test of every (lead, level, regime) cell with its transition counts, P(hit | hit) and P(hit | no hit) with Wilson 95% intervals, by lead, by level (q05/q95 and q01/q99), by regime
tables.spacing: the independence test of each cell read at spacing s = h, h + 1 and h + 2 (every s-th decision day of the regime's rows, phase 0), the Kupiec tests as in the design, Holm over the same 200 tests: how many independence rejections remain at each spacing. s = h is the design; s = h + 1 leaves no shared unknown innovation between two thinned forecasts under the 'two panel days' rule
tables.lag_profile: lift at lag k = 1..6 of the hit indicator, per lead and level: observed pairs (hit at t and at t - k, same regime, panel days k apart) over the pairs expected under each regime's own hit rate; 90% stationary-bootstrap interval (mean block 10, 2000 resamples, seed 1523) over the pairs in date order. Lift 1 is independence; the regime's own rate is held fixed in the expectation, so a lift above 1 at long lags is a miss rate that moves inside a regime
tables.day_types: lead 1, four levels: hit rate by target-day type (the ten types of candidate_calibration_1363.DAY_TYPES; types overlap) and by pressure-day type with Wilson 95% intervals and sizes; the share of hits and of hit-after-hit pairs on days that are neither calendar nor pressure days; lift at lag 1 on pairs of two ordinary days (type ordinary, pressure ordinary) against pairs with a calendar or pressure day; runs of consecutive hits (length distribution) and whether the hits of the 2021-23 regime sit in a few quarters
tables.drivers: lead 1: the standardised error z = (y - median) / ((q75 - q25) / 1.349); Pearson correlation of z at t with z at t - k, k = 1..6, and of |z| with |z| (scale), each with a stationary-bootstrap 90% interval; the slope of z on the last public spread's gap to the median ((y_{t-2} - median_t) / scale, level adaptation, public); the hit rate after a large public |z| (> 2) against otherwise; by regime. Lag 1 is marked not public
tables.simulation: a forecaster that is calibrated by construction and knows an AR(1) spread's dynamics, with phi in {0.3, 0.6, 0.9}, reads data to the panel day D - 1 for a target D + h (the two-row information lag) and also, as a control, to D. 1,855 days, 300 paths, seed 1523, one regime, no ties. Reported: mean lag-1 lift at lead 1 and the share of paths where the design's independence test at s = h and at s = h + 1 rejects at 5% (unadjusted), at q05 and q95, leads 1..3. It says whether the dependence the design flags is what a calibrated forecaster with this information lag shows, not what the candidate shows

adjustments.what: three post-hoc adjustments of the candidate's own quantile output, evaluated to estimate the effect a model change of that kind could have. They are not models: nothing is fitted to the walk's outcomes except the online rules below, which use only outcomes public at each decision day, and nothing is registered or proposed as a fitted parameter set. The page reports them as estimates of expected effect only
adjustments.public_error: e_pub(D) = y(D - 1) - median of the candidate's lead-1 forecast for target D - 1 (made on decision day D - 2). It is the latest lead-1 error public at decision day D. A decision day without one (the first two) is left unadjusted. The resolved cells of lead h at decision day D are the cells (D', h) whose target position is at most D - 1
adjustments.A1_recentre: q' = q + beta_h * e_pub(D) for every grid quantile of lead h; beta_h = clamp(sum(e_pub(D') * e(D', h)) / sum(e_pub(D')^2), 0, 1) over the resolved cells of lead h with an e_pub (expanding window); beta_h = 0 until 100 cells are resolved. Targets the level that adapts too slowly
adjustments.A2_rescale: q' = m + kappa_h * (q - m) with m the forecast's median; kappa_h = clamp(mean |e| / mean s_fc over the last 60 resolved cells of lead h, 0.7, 1.5), where s_fc is the forecast's own mean absolute deviation about its median (the grid quantiles weighted by half the gap between neighbouring levels, the weights normalised); kappa_h = 1 until 30 cells are resolved. Targets the scale that adapts too slowly
adjustments.A3_both: A1's shift, then A2's rescaling about the shifted median, where the realised errors that A2 reads are the errors of the A3 forecasts themselves, as made online
adjustments.settings_tuned: none: beta clamp, the 100 and 30 cell minimums, the window of 60, the clamp of kappa and the half-gap weights were fixed above before any adjusted score, and are not varied
adjustments.reads: grid CRPS (scoring_protocol.grid_crps) averaged over all cells (h = 1..5 equally weighted, as the primary score), paired against the unadjusted candidate on the same cells, 90% stationary-bootstrap interval (mean block 10 decision days, 2000 resamples, seed 1523) of the mean daily difference, pooled, by lead, by regime and by pressure-day type of the target; upper-tail twCRPS is also paired; and the design's coverage verdict (Holm rejections of 200, and which cells) on the adjusted forecasts. Also the same reads on the decision days after the first 250 (the online rules' warm-up)

not_here: no new model is fitted or registered; the 2026 days, B1, B1', B2, B4 and the uncapped secondary version are not read; a gate or spacing change is not adopted (the spacing table says what it would do, the choice is hers)

amendments.when: after the first score of this pull request was computed, before any of the added items was
amendments.why: the first score showed (a) hits on ordinary target days at well under half the regime-expected rate and on calendar or pressure days above it, with 73% of lead-1 target days non-ordinary, so a lift taken against the regime's rate alone overstates dependence that a day-type rate difference between adjacent days would produce; (b) a public lag-2 error that correlates negatively with the target's error (so A1, clamped at beta >= 0, can do nothing at lead 1); (c) a standardised absolute error that autocorrelates strongly at the public lags (so a scale that reacts faster than A2's 60 cells is the natural next arm)

added.tadj_lift: the lift at lags 1..6, leads 1..5, levels q05 and q95, with the expected pair value r_i * r_(i-k) from a multiplicative rate fitted in sample to that lead's hits by coordinate-wise iterative scaling on: the decision day's regime, each of the ten target-day types (membership) and each non-ordinary pressure-day type of the target. Same bootstrap as the lift. The fit is in sample (about 16 parameters on 100 to 130 hits), so this lift is biased a little downward; the page says so
added.A4_meanrevert: A1 with beta_h clamped to [-1, 1] instead of [0, 1], everything else as A1: the sign the first score showed at the public lag
added.A5_fast_rescale: A2 with the window of 20 resolved cells and the minimum of 10 instead of 60 and 30, everything else as A2
added.variant_count: 5 (A1, A2, A3 as declared, A4 and A5 added here); all five are reported, none is selected on its result, and no setting of any of them is varied

amendments.unchanged: A1, A2 and A3 and every setting declared above; the descriptive tables; the reads; no adjusted result of A4 or A5 existed when this entry was written
